context:
Goal: a push cannot skip the review of a branch another session handed in for review, without stopping normal pushes.
Problem (rule): no ruling says how strict the new push check must be when it cannot prove a review log, so the choice is yours.
Based on (read): the reviewer's report: merge/merge.py lines 5844 to 5845 allow a push with no review log, and hooks/guard_merge.py lines 1243 to 1247 allow it when the pull-request list read fails (a failed comment read refuses); the destination refusal at lines 1235 to 1237 runs before any pull-request read.
Based on (read): the lane's own note of this check (the recorded decision handed-in-push-needs-record) says 'Owner pick a', but the Explore agent found no such pick; the ruling guard-hooks-fail-closed (a missing guard script refuses; a guard that times out or crashes does not) says nothing about a failed read inside a guard.
Departs from: main — adds a check on pushes to handed-in branches.
Waiting on: the merge of the push check waits on your answer; triage's builder applies it and re-runs the review.
Meanwhile: the builder fixes the two findings that need no ruling (a glossary-banned name 'review record' in new code, and missing test cases).

options.gain: No false stops on normal pushes.
options.how: A push with no review log, a failed pull-request read, and an unnameable destination are each allowed with a one-line warning.
options.label: Keep it as built: let all three through, with a stderr line
options.lose: A push past a reviewed head with no log goes through; the step's stated rule ('refused until the log exists') is not enforced.

options.gain: A push cannot skip the review; this is the step's original guard.
options.how: Refuse a push with no review log, refuse when the pull-request list cannot be read, and refuse an unnameable destination.
options.label: Refuse all three until proven
options.lose: A failed read or a variable destination stops a normal push (false stops); lanes need your override more often.

options.gain: Stops the harm the step names (a push past a review) with the fewest false stops.
options.how: When a pull request is found for the branch and no review log exists for its last round, refuse; a failed pull-request read, or a destination that cannot be named, is allowed with a stderr line.
options.label: Refuse only a push with no review log when a pull request exists; allow the other two with a warning (recommended)
options.lose: A push slips through on a failed read or an unnameable destination, with only a warning.

ref: review round 1 (haiku reviewer) on branch handed-in-push-needs-record-2, 19:50 CST Nov 18, and an Explore agent's read of the rulings (none settles these four points); both are agent reads, not re-read by triage

Refuse only a push with no review log when a pull request exists; allow the other two with a warning (recommended)

title: How strict should the handed-in push check be when it cannot prove a review log?
why: c refuses the one push the step exists to stop and keeps normal pushes moving; a refuses nothing, b refuses on every failed read. Recommended by triage, not owner-typed.
